title: A moving clock's ticks, timed from outside
spoken: Coordinate time between a moving clock's ticks is gamma times its proper elapsed time.
explanation: Between two ticks of a moving clock, the stationary system's clocks record gamma times what the moving clock itself records. At 0.6c a clock shows 0.8 s while 1 s passes in the stationary system.
assumptions: A clock and a rod at rest in the moving system, which moves at speed v relative to the stationary system, with |v| < c.
The clock's two ticks happen at the same place in its own rest frame; the rod's two ends are located at the same time in the stationary system.
Modern teaching notation: Delta tau is the modern proper time, the time one clock records. It is not the paper's tau, which is the moving system's time coordinate.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: A comparison of two measurements of the same pair of ticks. It does not say the clock's mechanism has slowed in its own frame.

notes.title: Gamma times the clock's own time
notes.explanation: Gamma is at least 1, so the stationary system's time between the ticks is never shorter than the clock's.

notes.title: Time between the ticks, stationary system
notes.explanation: Found from two stationary clocks at the two places the ticks happen, synchronized by the section 1 rule.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: One over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared: 1 at rest, larger at any speed, without limit as v approaches c. The paper writes it as beta.

notes.title: Time the moving clock records
notes.explanation: What the moving clock itself shows between the two ticks, which happen at one place in its own rest frame.

sentence.text: The stationary system's time between the ticks
the time the moving clock records
